description: Group tax and transfer pricing functions of multinationals with 5 to 500+ legal entities that must produce OECD BEPS Action 13 three-tiered documentation (Master File, Local Files, Country-by-Country Reporting) every fiscal year in dozens of countries. Reptune reference customers in this group include TomTom, Stahl, Avnet, Ravago and Stanley Black & Decker, among more than 150 multinationals worldwide. The group spans the buyer who owns the transfer pricing policy and budget, the coordinator who runs the annual documentation cycle on the platform, and the local finance contacts in each country who supply data, review the local file and face the local tax authority.

customers.name: Group Head of Tax / Transfer Pricing Director
customers.description: Owns the global transfer pricing policy of a multinational with 20 to 500+ legal entities in 15 to 60 countries, such as a Dutch technology group, a Benelux chemicals or plastics distributor or a US industrial with European headquarters. Sets the group's transfer pricing methods, functional profiles and target margins, budgets the compliance cycle, selects the platform, plan and service level (On Demand, Collaborative or Full Service), and signs off the Master File, Local Files and CbCR before they go out. Answers to the CFO and the audit committee on tax risk, defends the group in tax audits, Advance Pricing Agreements and Mutual Agreement Procedures, and is judged on whether documentation exists everywhere it is required, what it costs per entity, and how many adjustments and penalties the group absorbs. Works with a small in-house team, local finance controllers and a handful of external advisers.

jobsToBeDone.name: Be audit-ready in every country without a documentation project each year
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Maintain a Master File, Local Files and supporting evidence (functional analyses, benchmarks, intercompany agreements, segmented financials) that are current, consistent and locally compliant in every country where the group exceeds a threshold, so that an audit, an APA negotiation or a MAP can be answered from what already exists. The job is to make documentation a by-product of a maintained transfer pricing model rather than an annual scramble with advisers.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Every in-scope entity has a final, localised Local File before its local deadline, the Master File and Local Files tell one consistent story backed by signed agreements and current benchmarks, and audit information requests are answered from the archive within the authority's deadline with no documentation-related adjustment.

steps.step: Codify the global transfer pricing policy in one model

Review the model whenever the business changes: a restructuring, an acquisition, a new principal structure or a new intercompany service.

customerJourneyStories.name: From adviser-prepared binders to an audit-ready platform
customerJourneyStories.summary: A Head of Tax at a Dutch-headquartered industrial group with about 60 entities in 25 countries moves the group's transfer pricing documentation from a Big 4 adviser's annual project to Reptune.net, from the audit that exposed the gaps to the renewal in which the group takes most of the work in-house.

stages.narrative: An Italian tax audit asks for the Local File of a distribution entity and the group discovers that the adviser's file is 18 months old, in English, and describes a functional profile that the restructured entity no longer has. The adviser quotes a six-figure fee to refresh all 25 countries. The CFO asks the Head of Tax for a way to keep documentation current every year at a predictable cost.

At a Dutch tax directors' network meeting the Head of Tax hears a peer describe how Reptune.net generates Local Files from one transfer pricing model and that its documentation 'saved the day' in several audits. A look at the reptune.tax site shows named customers such as TomTom, Stahl, Avnet and Ravago, 170+ countries covered, and a free two-week trial with no installation.

The Head of Tax compares Reptune against keeping the adviser, a Big 4 documentation tool and a generic document-automation suite. Decisive checks are whether the group's policy fits the rule-based model, the localised templates for Italy and other high-risk countries, the fixed rate per Local File under Full Service, the ISO 27001 certification and SSO for IT security review, and the fact that the same platform allows the group to move to On Demand later. References from two comparable groups and a pricing proposal per plan and service level settle the choice.

During the two-week trial the transfer pricing manager loads entities and transactions via Excel bulk entry with the R-AI onboarding assistant, and Reptune specialists configure the model for the largest division. The first generated Local File for the Italian entity, in the localised template and machine-translated with the glossary, is reviewed by the local adviser and passes with minor comments. The group signs an Advanced plan with Full Service for the first cycle.

In the first cycle Reptune specialists deliver 40 Local Files and the Master File while the in-house team monitors progress on the dashboard. The Head of Tax uses the world map and deadline view in the quarterly audit committee meeting, moves the benchmark studies and intercompany agreements into the platform, and starts using the included expert hours for a value chain analysis rather than for file production.

At renewal the group reports compliance cost per entity down by more than half and the Italian audit closed without a documentation-related adjustment. The Head of Tax switches 30 entities to Collaborative, keeps Full Service for the ten highest-risk countries, adds the CbCR module and the Legal Module, and agrees to act as a reference for the next group that considers the move.

customerJourneyStories.name: Expanding from Local Files to CbCR, Legal Module and risk analytics
customerJourneyStories.summary: Two cycles into using Reptune.net for Master File and Local Files, the Head of Tax of a US-listed group's European region extends the platform to CbCR and EU Public CbCR, the Legal Module and risk management, so the audit committee sees the whole picture from one source.

stages.narrative: The group's first EU Public CbCR under Directive (EU) 2021/2101 is due, the CbCR XML is still prepared by a corporate adviser from a spreadsheet, and the audit committee asks for a single tax risk report across documentation, CbCR and intercompany agreements. Legal keeps the agreements in a share drive and cannot say which transactions are uncovered.

In the annual account review the Reptune specialist shows that the CbCR module generates filing-ready XML and Excel and EU Public CbCR in XHTML with inline XBRL from the same data, and that the Legal Module links signed agreements and signatories to the transactions already in the model. A Reptune webinar on CbCR risk analysis and the Pillar Two transitional safe harbour makes the risk use case concrete.

The Head of Tax checks with the corporate secretary whether the Legal Module can replace the entity register and DocuSign workflow, has IT confirm that custom user profiles and location-restricted access satisfy the group's access policy, and compares the Enterprise plan with the CbCR add-on against continuing with the adviser for CbCR alone. The ability to run a CbCR risk analysis and the safe-harbour test in the same place tips the decision.

The prior year's CbCR is re-created in the platform from the adviser's spreadsheet and validated against the filed XML; the Actions Required page catches two constituent entities with inconsistent jurisdiction codes. Legal loads the entities and 120 intercompany agreements, and the first structure chart and agreement coverage report go to the Head of Tax within a month.

CbCR, notifications and EU Public CbCR are filed from the platform, risk indicators per country are reviewed monthly with the regional tax managers, and new agreements are generated, signed through DocuSign and archived against their transactions. The quarterly audit committee pack is now a dashboard export with coverage, deadlines, risk and agreement status.

The group upgrades to Enterprise with divisions for its two business units, standardises on Reptune for the Americas region as well, and the Head of Tax presents the setup at an industry conference as the model for continuous compliance. The account becomes one of Reptune's largest and a design partner for the R-AI country-expert mode.

The job is to make the model complete and correct enough that generated Local Files need no manual changes in the exported files.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: The model is live within days of starting, covers every entity and transaction type in scope, generates Master File and Local Files that are consistent with each other and with the policy, and needs only incremental maintenance when the business changes.

customerJourneyStories.name: Trial in two weeks, first cycle in one season
customerJourneyStories.summary: A transfer pricing manager at a Benelux distribution group with 45 entities in 20 countries, previously running the cycle in Word and Excel with a local adviser per country, goes from a free two-week trial to running the whole fiscal-year cycle in Reptune.net with the Collaborative service level.

stages.narrative: The previous cycle ended with two Local Files finalised after their deadlines, a Polish file in a format the local adviser had to rebuild, and a functional analysis that differed between the Master File and three Local Files because each had been edited separately. The Head of Tax asks the manager to propose a way to run the next cycle without repeating this.

The manager searches for transfer pricing documentation software, reads the reptune.tax feature pages on the automated report generator, workflow and country regulations, and watches a demo in which a Local File for Italy is generated in the localised template. A former Big 4 colleague now at Avnet confirms the group has used the platform globally since 2019.

Together with the Head of Tax the manager compares Reptune with a Big 4 tool and with continuing in Word. The decisive points are that the model is rule-based and generates every file from one source, that deadlines and thresholds are maintained for all 20 countries, that machine translation with glossaries is included as an add-on, and that the Advanced plan with Collaborative service keeps Reptune specialists involved for the first cycle. IT signs off on ISO 27001 and SSO.

In the two-week trial the manager loads all 45 entities via Excel bulk entry, defines four company types and eight transaction types with the R-AI onboarding assistant, uploads last year's benchmarks, and generates a draft Local File for the Dutch principal and the Polish distributor. Validation flags twelve missing data points that would have surfaced in December; the drafts read consistently. The group signs.

The first cycle is scoped in the platform, data tasks go to 20 local contacts with automatic reminders, Reptune specialists draft the Master File and the manager generates the Local Files, localises them with the templates and machine translation, and tracks progress on the dashboard. The Head of Tax sees the world map turn green country by country instead of asking for status by e-mail.

The cycle closes with every file final before its deadline and preparation time per Local File down by more than half. For the next fiscal year the manager moves to On Demand for most entities, keeps Collaborative for five countries, adds the R-AI Country Expert add-on, and rolls the scope forward in the platform in an afternoon.

customerJourneyStories.name: From English-only files to localisation, translation and AI writing
customerJourneyStories.summary: A documentation coordinator at a US-headquartered group's European tax team, already generating English Local Files in Reptune.net, adopts localised templates, machine translation, AI-assisted writing and the R-AI country expert to stop depending on local advisers for every non-English country.

stages.narrative: Local advisers in Italy, Spain and Brazil each return the English Local File translated and rewritten in their own style, the invoices for translation and 'localisation review' exceed the platform subscription, and a Spanish audit notes that the local file terminology does not match the intercompany agreement.

The coordinator reads a Reptune release note on machine translation into 28 languages with transfer pricing glossaries and the coming R-AI Local Requirements mode, and asks the Reptune specialist during a support call how other groups handle Italy and Brazil. The specialist shows the Italian localised template and a glossary-driven translation side by side with the adviser's version.

The coordinator tests translation quality on one Local File with the Spanish local contact, checks that the glossary carries the group's defined terms into all languages, confirms which countries still require human-certified translation, and models the cost of the machine translation add-on against last year's translation invoices. The Head of Tax approves the add-on and the R-AI Country Expert.

Italy, Spain and Brazil run through the new path for one cycle: localised template where available, machine translation with the glossary, local contact review in the platform, certified translation ordered only for Brazil. Local advisers are asked to review, not rewrite, and their review comments drop to a page each.

All non-English countries move to the localised path, AI-assisted writing is used to draft entity-specific custom text from the model's facts, and the coordinator uses R-AI to answer local-requirement questions before asking an adviser. Translation and localisation cost per Local File falls and the narrative stays consistent across languages.

At renewal the group keeps the add-ons, asks Reptune for two more localised templates, and the coordinator joins the customer panel that tests the R-AI Local Requirements mode, giving the group early access to country-expert answers in the platform.

customers.name: Local Finance Controller / Country Tax Contact
customers.description: The finance controller, accountant or country tax contact of a single legal entity (or a country cluster) within a multinational, who is asked once a year by group tax to provide the entity's financials, segmented P&L and intercompany transaction data, to review the Local File from the local perspective, to arrange translation and local forms, to file or lodge the documentation with the local tax authority, and to respond when the local tax authority audits the entity. Transfer pricing is a small part of the job next to statutory accounts, VAT and local tax returns; the controller wants a clear request, a template that matches the ERP extract, minimal back-and-forth with headquarters, and documentation that protects the entity when the local auditor comes. Judged locally on filing on time and on audit outcomes, and by group tax on the quality and timeliness of the data provided.
careAbout: A clear, scoped data request with a deadline, a template that matches what the ERP can produce, and no repeated questions from headquarters
Validation at upload time that tells the controller what is wrong before group tax finds it weeks later
A segmented P&L per activity and transaction that reconciles to the statutory accounts, so the numbers in the Local File are the numbers the auditor will see
A Local File in the local language and format, with the local forms, ready before the local filing or preparation deadline
Knowing the local threshold, deadline and procedure without having to research it or pay a local adviser
Documentation and evidence that can be pulled up in an hour when the local tax authority asks, so an audit does not become a reconstruction exercise
winsThem: Excel data exchange templates with built-in validation and, where set up, direct ERP integration so the entity's data flows in without re-keying
Task assignments with e-mail reminders that tell the controller exactly what is due, for which entity, by when, in the platform rather than in a long e-mail thread
Local Files generated in the localised template and machine-translated into the local language with the group glossary, plus local forms and procedures per country
R-AI country-expert answers and Reptune specialists who know the local requirements and can help when the local tax authority sends a request
An archive of the filed version with its data, agreements and benchmarks that the controller can show an auditor from the platform

jobsToBeDone.outcome: Audit requests are answered from the platform within the statutory period, the documentation and evidence are consistent and hold up, the entity avoids adjustments and penalties attributable to documentation, and lessons from the audit are reflected in the model for the following year.

customerJourneyStories.name: From e-mailed spreadsheets to guided data tasks
customerJourneyStories.summary: The finance controller of a Spanish distribution subsidiary of a Dutch group experiences the group's move to Reptune.net from the receiving end: from the annual e-mail with three spreadsheets and a Word file to a task in the platform with a validated template, a localised Local File and a filing record.

stages.narrative: Last year the controller sent segmented figures to headquarters three times because the spreadsheet format changed between requests, received the Local File in English two days before the Spanish deadline, and paid a local adviser to translate it overnight. The controller tells group tax that the process cannot be repeated with the same team.

Group tax announces that the group is moving to Reptune.net and invites the controller to a 45-minute onboarding webinar with a Reptune specialist, where the controller sees the data exchange template, the validation on upload and the Spanish translation with the group glossary. A colleague at another subsidiary says the templates matched their SAP extract.

The controller has no purchase decision but decides how much to trust the new process: checks that the template fields map to the entity's chart of accounts, asks whether local review happens in the platform or in Word, confirms that access is read-only for the entity's own data and via SSO, and asks group tax whether the Spanish threshold and deadline are tracked so the entity is not surprised again.

For the first cycle the controller receives a task with the entity's templates and deadline, uploads the ERP extract, corrects four validation findings in twenty minutes and submits. The draft Local File arrives in the platform six weeks before the deadline, in the localised template and in Spanish; the controller corrects two local facts in the review task rather than in a Word file.

In the second cycle the controller uses the ERP integration set up by group IT, so financials arrive without an upload, and uses R-AI to check the Spanish local form requirements. Reminders come from the platform, the filing record is kept there, and the controller spends under a day on transfer pricing for the year.

When group tax asks local contacts whether to keep the platform, the controller reports data effort down from days to hours and no missed Spanish deadline in two years, and asks group tax to add the Portuguese entity the controller also covers to the same process.

customerJourneyStories.name: The audit that made the local controller a believer
customerJourneyStories.summary: The country tax contact of a German manufacturing entity of a US group, initially sceptical of headquarters' documentation platform, faces a German transfer pricing audit and comes to rely on Reptune.net's archive, evidence and specialist support, becoming the entity's advocate for filing everything from the platform.

stages.narrative: The German tax office announces a Betriebsprüfung covering three fiscal years and requests the transfer pricing documentation within the statutory period. The contact has the English Local Files from headquarters on a share drive, is unsure which version was final for each year, and cannot find the signed toll manufacturing agreement.

Group tax points the contact to the entity's page in Reptune.net, where each fiscal year's filed Local File, its German translation, the data snapshot, the linked agreements and benchmarks and the filing record are archived. The Head of Tax mentions that another group's VP Taxation said the platform 'saved the day' in audits and offers Reptune specialist hours for controversy support.

The contact checks that the archived versions match what was handed to the tax office, that the German translation uses the terminology in the agreements, that the segmented P&L reconciles to the HGB accounts, and that the specialists have German audit experience. Satisfied, the contact decides to run the audit response from the platform rather than rebuild a file with a local adviser.

The first information request is answered within the deadline from the archive: filed Local Files, the agreement retrieved from the Legal Module with its signatories, the benchmark range and the entity's tested result per year. A Reptune specialist reviews the response with group tax; the auditor's follow-up questions narrow to one transaction.

Through the audit the contact tracks every request and response in the platform, uses R-AI to check German documentation rules on deadlines and penalties, and works with group tax to adjust the entity's functional profile in the model for the year in progress. The audit closes with no adjustment attributable to documentation.

The contact asks group tax to include the German entity's CbCR notification and local forms in the platform workflow, files the next Local File from the platform with the certified translation ordered through it, and tells the other German entities' controllers to do the same.
